title: Bailly Cemetery Near Chesterton: The Graveyard That Was Buried in Sand

sources.what: earliest non-Indigenous cemetery in Porter County; first burial Napoleon 'Robert' 1827; wooden fence 1866; at least three Swedish immigrants buried 1869-74; six-foot limestone wall topped with iron spikes, 1885; 1914 Frances Rose Howe, Joseph's granddaughter, had local builder Theodore Stephens encase the wall in concrete and fill it with sand, the cemetery 'beneath seven feet of earth'; a letter reversed on the plaque

first recorded burial about 1827; six-foot limestone wall topped with iron spikes; Frances R. Howe 'had Theodore Stephens of Chesterton construct a concrete block wall around the old one'; interior filled with sand
sources.who: Wikipedia, Bailly Cemetery (citing Schiemann, 1952, and the Chesterton Tribune, 1949)

sources.what: Bailly entered northern Indiana in 1822; Swedish immigrants buried there; Howe 'contracted with Theodore Stephens of Chesterton' (ca. 1913); concrete between the walls
sources.who: NPS Historic Structure Report, 1976, via Historical Images of Porter County

sources.what: 'a six-foot high stone wall, iron spiked'; 'the old walled cemetery was filled with sand'; 'The bronze N ... is placed backward in the plaque'
sources.who: Theodore Stephens, 'Bailly Cemetery - Roman Style' (1956), via Historical Images of Porter County

sources.what: Bailly Cemetery Trail, a 0.6-mile round-trip extension from the Bailly-Chellberg trail; sections may be closed

beats.text: In Porter, next to Chesterton, in the Indiana Dunes, there's a cemetery that was buried on purpose.
beats.label: PORTER, NEAR CHESTERTON

beats.text: Fur trader Joseph Bailly settled here in the 1820s, and burials on this sand ridge go back at least that far.
beats.label: THE 1820s
beats.credit: National Park Service; NPS Historic Structure Report (1976)

beats.text: Neighbors buried their dead there too, including Swedish immigrants.
beats.label: NEIGHBORS TOO
beats.credit: National Park Service; NPS Historic Structure Report (1976)

beats.text: In the 1880s, the family walled it in with stone, six feet high and topped with iron spikes.
beats.label: THE WALL
beats.credit: National Park Service; Wikipedia; Theodore Stephens (1956)

beats.text: Around 1914, granddaughter Frances Howe hired a Chesterton builder to wrap the walls in concrete and fill the inside with sand.
beats.label: AROUND 1914
beats.credit: National Park Service; Wikipedia; NPS report (1976); Stephens (1956)

beats.text: The family's graves are still under that sand. And on a copy of the plaque, one letter is backward.
beats.label: FAMILY GRAVES STILL THERE

beats.text: Today it's part of Indiana Dunes National Park, and a short trail leads up to it.
beats.label: INDIANA DUNES NATIONAL PARK

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.

factcheck.result: Lines 2-5 and 7 supported. Line 1 now 'In Porter, next to Chesterton'; 'old graves' became 'the family's graves' (other remains found in 1914 were moved outside); the backward letter is on a copy of the plaque; year card 'filled with sand'; obelisk/rows and lakeshore dune drawings replaced (the site is a walled platform on an inland wooded ridge).
